summary: Shelby County lookout listed as removed in a Tennessee tower inventory; no other source found on its history.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

evidence.supports: Shelby County, 433 ft elevation, district-tower 9-18, removed
9-18 is a district-tower number from a 1976 list of state forest towers
evidence.quote: Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from 1976 list of towers

evidence.supports: CCC erected 98 lookout towers in Tennessee, 1933-1941
evidence.quote: From 1933 to 1941, the Civilian Conservation Corps erected 98 lookout towers in Tennessee.

evidence.supports: the inventory's name is Shelby S.F.; tower listed as removed
many towers removed; most former locations private property
evidence.quote: Many have been removed, and most locations are now private property

evidence.supports: Meeman-Shelby Forest State Park is a state park in Shelby County near Memphis
evidence.quote: Meeman-Shelby Forest State Park is a state park in Shelby County, Tennessee near Memphis

notes_for_editor: One source for the tower: a personal, unofficial inventory whose author says some names are their own. No build, design, staffing or fire record found. 'Shelby S.F.' is not explained by any source read. The record point (35.3439, -90.0292) is about 320 m east of Wikipedia's coordinates for Meeman-Shelby Forest State Park (35.3439, -90.0327), so the tower may stand in the park, but no source says so; the story does not link them. A 2015 consultant history, 'Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933-1975', appeared in search results but was not read; it may settle the name and fate. No correction proposed.
